## Where the content comes from

The app is built from the course's own material:

- the **session slides** by Qinyun Lin (sessions 1–4 and 6, preliminary "v0" versions; Session 5 was a computer lab, Session 7 a guest lecture whose slides are not yet in the course folder);
- the instructor's **Canvas posts** for each session: topics, learning objectives and key questions;
- the **course syllabus** (learning outcomes, examination) and the **literature list**;
- the links in the Canvas posts and slides, collected on [Resources](resources.qmd) (videos, books, web pages);
- **lecture notes** taken in class (topics marked ✏️; they also record that the exam tests concepts, not programming).

Explanations, quizzes, drills, simulated figures, R cells, why-questions and written model answers were written for this app. Simulations use made-up data. The course books are cited, not reproduced:

- Lawson, Banerjee, Haining & Ugarte (eds.) (2016). *Handbook of Spatial Epidemiology*. CRC Press. Main textbook.
- Anselin (2024). *An Introduction to Spatial Data Science with GeoDa, Volume 1: Exploring Spatial Data*. Chapman & Hall/CRC. Chapters 1–7, 10, 13, 16.

Neither book has been used for this version of the app yet.

## How the badges were assigned

| Badge | Rule |
|---|---|
| <span class="flag-badge flag-objective">🎯 Instructor learning objective</span> | The section teaches something stated as a learning objective: in the **course syllabus** (Session 1: role of place, spatial dependence and heterogeneity, bias from aggregation, measurement and missing data), the **Canvas post** (Sessions 2, 4, 5 and 6) or the **"Learning goals" slide** (Session 3) |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-keyq">❓ Instructor's key question</span> | The section answers one of the **key questions** in the Session 4 Canvas post, or a question the instructor asked on a slide (for example "which is the box map?", "is π̂ the average of all rates?", the SAR plausibility and scenario slides; in Session 6 "what pattern do you see?", "which is the larger bandwidth?", "does a spatial lag represent a causal spillover?", "can a neighbouring municipality serve as a control?") |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-notes">✏️ Emphasised in class</span> | Written down in the lecture notes: spatial file types, DeSO, geocoding, polygon/area, GIS and GeoDa, the social-ecological and life-course models, and the lab recap of SAR, SEM and Wy (Session 5). Where a noted topic also matches an objective (MAUP, the definition, SAR vs SEM), 🎯 is used |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-inferred">📌 Likely exam-relevant (AI-inferred)</span> | Inferred from definitions, formulas and worked examples on the slides. **Not confirmed** |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-optional">📎 Optional depth</span> | Marked "optional depth" on the slide (PC priors), listed as not covered (Session 3 scope slide), or stated as not expected (INLA's computational details) |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-seminar">🗣️ Mini-project</span> | One section per group question in the compulsory mini-project (Session 8), from the Canvas post. Counted as exam-relevant on the dashboard, because each question is also a core course concept |

## Course facts

STA530 Spatial Epidemiology, 3.5 credits, Sahlgrenska Academy, University of Gothenburg. Autumn 2026, 1 October – 3 November, 50% pace, taught in English.

| Examination | Credits | Grades |
|---|---|---|
| Individual written exam | 2.5 | U / G / VG |
| Active participation in a seminar | 1.0 | U / G |

To pass the course you need G on both; VG on the course needs VG on the written exam.

Software: R (with RStudio or Positron) and **GeoDa**, to be installed before 13 October.

## Notes on the slides

- Session 3, slide 12 (toy SAR example): the slide shows a direct impact of about 1.019 and indirect impacts of about 0.116. The exact inverse of (I − 0.2W) gives 1.023 and 0.114. The total, 1.25 = β/(1 − ρ), agrees. The app uses the exact values.
- Session 6: the slides give no formulas for the gravity potential or the two-step floating catchment area method; the app uses the standard forms from the cited literature (Luo & Qi 2009; Bryant & Delamater 2019). The risk-classification thresholds in [5.6](session5.qmd#t5-6) come from Richardson et al. (2004), not from the slides.
- Sessions 5 and 8 cover the computer lab and the mini-project as concepts on made-up data only, never as solutions.
- Session 7 is built from the Canvas description only; it will be completed when the guest lecture slides are added.
- The slides are preliminary ("v0") versions. If updated slides are posted, sections may be revised.

## Your progress data

Your review status (Not reviewed / Reviewed / Confident) is stored in this browser's localStorage under the key `sta530_topic_status`. It stays between visits on the same browser and device, but not across devices or after clearing site data. Use **Export progress** on the [dashboard](dashboard.qmd) to keep a backup.
